claims.text: DFT-based simulations of metal-oxide interfaces can predict the oxidation resistance of metallic materials.
The proposed prediction applies under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
The metallic materials are initially in a pristine state.
Metal-oxide interfaces are the structural mediator relevant to oxidation resistance.
Oxidation resistance is governed through oxidation-reaction kinetics and thermodynamics.
The proposed method will yield a 20% improvement in oxidation resistance relative to baseline.
The baseline is the oxidation resistance of metallic materials without DFT-based simulations.
The applicable oxygen partial-pressure range is 10^-5–10^-3 atm.
DFT prediction accuracy may be limited by the selected exchange-correlation functional.
DFT prediction accuracy may be limited by the quality of the metal-oxide interface model.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes DFT as a predictive method, but the outcome and baseline imply that merely performing DFT simulations physically improves oxidation resistance by 20%. A simulation can predict or guide a material modification, but no actual composition, coating, or processing intervention that would cause improved resistance is specified.

The predicted outcome concerns a 20% improvement over baseline, whereas the falsification rule instead tests whether a prediction agrees with a measured value within 10%; these are different propositions.
